summary: 11:30 PM ET run, published at 12:06 AM ET. Rams 28, Giants 6, and week 2 is complete. All three Monday props lost: Terrance Ferguson went for 54 receiving yards against our under 32.5, Theo Johnson caught nothing on four targets against our over 8.5, and Devin Singletary ran three times for 9 yards against our over 15.5. None of them left hurt, so all three are straight losses at a full unit. That closes NFL week 2 at 7-10 and plus 1.01 units, carried entirely by two researched picks and a parlay while the prop leans went 2-7 and lost 4.23 units. The weekly review is below and it is not kind to the prop programme.

props.title: Terrance Ferguson UNDER 32.5 receiving yards
props.actual: 6 catches on 9 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown, long of 20. Played the whole game and was not on the post-game injury report.
props.settlementReason: 54 receiving yards is over the 32.5 line, so the under loses at the published price. Nine targets was the most of any Rams tight end and the second most on the team, which is what losing Puka Nacua, Jordan Whittington and CJ Daniels to the inactive list does to a tight end's volume. We flagged this at 12:19 PM, again at 6:10 PM and again at 7:29 PM while the pick was live. It was still the wrong side.
props.why: Prop lean on our number alone: our projection is 16.3 against 32.5 and the under reads 81.9% on the raw curve, which has no graded history against a line yet, so the true chance is lower than that. Our number is 16.3 yards against a 32.5 line, and the Rams' tight end room splits targets with Colby Parkinson. The role is settled by last season rather than by this season's single game.
props.risk: Uncalibrated chance one game into the season, and yesterday six of these went 2-4. A tight end line turns on one target. Confidence 2 of 10.

props.title: Theo Johnson OVER 8.5 receiving yards
props.entryNote: Closed to new entries at 7:22 PM ET: the receiving line was 9.5 at BetMGM, DraftKings, ESPN BET and FanDuel and no book still offered 8.5. The published cutoff closes at 9 or higher.
props.actual: 4 targets, no catches, 0 receiving yards. Played the whole game and was not on the post-game injury report.
props.settlementReason: Zero receiving yards is under the 8.5 line, so the over loses at the published price. He was targeted four times and caught none of them. This was the one pick of the three that beat the closing line, by a yard, and it still lost by nine: a clean reminder that closing line value is a measure of the number we got and not of the outcome.
props.why: Prop lean on our number alone: our projection is 26.5 against 8.5 and the over reads 79.1% on the raw curve, which has no graded history against a line yet, so the true chance is lower than that. Our number is 26.5 yards against an 8.5 line; the Giants' tight end has been a steady short-area target. The role is settled by last season rather than by this season's single game.

props.title: Devin Singletary OVER 15.5 rushing yards
props.actual: 3 carries for 9 yards, long of 6, plus one target and no catch. Played and was not on the post-game injury report.
props.settlementReason: Nine rushing yards is under the 15.5 line, so the over loses at the published price. The Giants split the backfield four ways: Cam Skattebo 12 carries, Najee Harris 4, Singletary 3. Harris came off the inactive list active at 6:56 PM and the market took the rushing line from 15.5 down to between 9.5 and 12.5 across five books before kickoff. The close at 10.5 was right and our published 15.5 was five yards the wrong side of it, the worst closing line value of any pick this season.

weeklyReview: Picks: NFL week 2 closed 7-10 for plus 1.01 units on 16.25 units risked, a 6.2% return. Two researched picks went 2-0 for plus 2.03 (Jahmyr Gibbs over 29.5 receiving yards, Sam LaPorta over 4.5 receptions). Parlays went 1-1 for plus 3.35, the four-player volume ticket winning a full unit at plus 3.60 and the Sunday longshot losing its quarter. Model leans on totals went 2-2 for minus 0.14, which is what break-even looks like. Prop leans went 2-7 and lost 4.23 units, and that is the whole of the week's damage.

Against the closing line over 15 games, the side our number favoured went 8-7 and the over-under call went 6-9. Average margin miss 12.57 against the close's 12.23, average total miss 10.70 against its 10.23. We were the closer estimator on the margin 8 times in 15 and on the total only 5 times in 15. Two weeks in, our NFL numbers are level with the market on sides and behind it on totals. 80% of finals landed inside our 80% range and the Brier score is 0.2502.

The finding of the week is in the prop table, not the win-loss. Across 538 graded player markets this season the book's line is closer to the result than our projection in six of seven markets. On receiving yards, 158 graded, our projection misses by 22.94 yards against the line's 20.58 and we are closer only 66 times in 158, which is 42%. Rushing yards: ours 17.45, the line 16.36. Receptions: 1.62 against 1.53. Passing yards: 64.89 against 62.73. Carries: 3.35 against 3.17. Completions is the one market where we are ahead, 4.83 against 4.90.

Put those two things together and the prop lean programme has been publishing mostly receiving yards, which is the market where our projection is furthest behind the closing line. A 60% raw read on a number that is worse than the book's number is not an edge. The rule should change: no prop lean on receiving yards until the projection beats the close in that market, and the 538-row table is the test.

Two projection errors showed up plainly on Monday and both point the same way. Theo Johnson projected 26.5 receiving yards on 3.5 targets while playing 46% of snaps behind Isaiah Likely, and caught none of his four targets. Devin Singletary projected 27.2 rushing yards as the third back in a four-way split, and ran three times for 9 yards. Both projections lean on last season's role; neither knows what this season's snap share is. Weighting a player's share by recent snaps rather than by last season's job is the change most likely to fix this.

Closing line value: 17 picks published this week, all 17 with a comparable close. Five beat the close, eight lost to it, four matched, average plus 0.06, which is nothing. All three Monday props were quoted off DraftKings alone before the other four books posted their player lines: Ferguson closed two yards against us, Singletary five yards against us, Theo Johnson one yard in our favour. The one-book rule added at lunchtime on Monday would have caught all three, and it stays.

Player chances are still published raw because there was no graded history to shrink them with. After two weeks there is a little: 2-7 on prop leans priced at raw reads between 60% and 86%. That is a small sample and a clear direction, and fitting a shrink factor for the player curve is now worth doing rather than waiting for the season to finish.
